candidates.visual_fit: A plausible late-80s/90s beige CRT in a moody room, with a clean, slow camera move and no people. It does not show a power-on, POST, memory count or OS. It can serve as a period-setting cutaway, not as the 'booting' shot.
candidates.hardware_date_evidence: CPU unverified and unverifiable from this clip. Re-checked on the acquired 4096x2160 file: no PC case, tower or chassis appears anywhere in frame, so no CPU is visible. No date, serial, BIOS text or OS is legible. The one marking that IS legible at full resolution is the monitor bezel: a 'ViewSonic' wordmark with the ViewSonic bird logo, and an 'E70' model marking. That identifies a monitor make and model, not a CPU, a system or a date, and is not Pentium evidence. At 720p neither marking is legible. Period-plausible set; boot not shown; CPU unverified.

Beige CRT monitor and beige keyboard on a dark wooden desk; pink rotary telephone, folding camera, glass flask, foil object and coloured booklets on the desk; two audio cassettes on top of the monitor; green metal chair back at left foreground; pendant lamp at top centre; poster taped to the wall at top right; wall sockets and cables below. CRT screen blank and dark.
Same set, camera drifted so the desk sits slightly right and the chair moved left. CRT screen still blank and dark.
Drift continues; monitor now centre-left, more of the right wall visible. CRT screen still blank and dark.
Composition reads clearly at 720p and the screen is unmistakably dark and blank. The ViewSonic wordmark and the E70 marking are NOT legible at this size.

candidates.boot_check_on_acquired_file: No boot and no power-on. Across the selected 0.5-10.5 s range the screen never lights or flickers; there is no POST, memory count, BIOS screen or OS, and nobody touches the machine. The only motion is the slow camera drift.
candidates.watermark_check_on_acquired_file: No watermark, baked-in caption or burned-in text in any inspected frame. Nothing was removed; the original is preserved byte-identical.
